title: Minimum Wage Us: Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual pay using the 38-hour week formula, plus tax, super, and tax. Minimum wage us Australians rely on the National Minimum Wage vs award

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your base hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a 38‑hour week, use 38. The formula gives annual gross = hourly × 38 × 52. For example, at $26.44/hour, that’s about $1,004.90/week or 2,009.80/fortnight. Super is 12% of ordinary earnings paid on top, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour (from 1 July 2026) set by the Fair Work Commission. Award rates are industry‑ or industry‑specific minimums set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. They can be higher than the National Minimum Wage. Casual loading is 25% on top of the base rate, so casual minimum is $33.05/hour. Always check your award or agreement.

faqs.q: How is superannuation paid on top of my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your base rate. It does not reduce your take‑home pay. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. For a full‑time worker at the National Minimum Wage, super adds about $120.59 per week to your retirement savings.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you earn an hourly rate, you can estimate your annual gross pay by multiplying that rate by the number of hours you work each week and then by 52 weeks. For a full‑time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It gives a rough annual figure that you can use to compare job offers or plan your budget.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you type your base hourly rate. If you are a casual employee, check the box to add 25% casual loading on top. Never type a rate that already includes casual loading – the calculator adds it for you. The result shows your annual gross, fortnightly pay, and estimated tax and super.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

Minimum wage us in Australia is set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is **$26.44 per hour**, which equals **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours. For casual workers, the 25% loading brings it to **$33.05 per hour**.

However, many employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets a higher minimum rate. Award rates vary by industry and job classification. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) that list the correct minimum rates for each award. Always check your award before relying on the National Minimum Wage.

### Casual Loading and Super

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of their base rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. This loading is added to the hourly rate before calculating annual pay. For example, a casual at the National Minimum Wage would have a loaded rate of $33.05/hour.

Superannuation guarantee is **12% of ordinary earnings**, paid on top of your base rate. It does not come out of your pay – your employer adds it separately. The super contribution stops once your earnings reach the **$270,830 maximum contribution base**.

## Estimating Your Take‑Home Pay

To estimate your weekly or fortnightly pay, start with your gross annual figure. Then deduct tax using the 2026‑27 resident tax scale:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- Over $190,000: 45%

Medicare levy generally 2% (using the 2025‑26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026‑27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here).

For a full‑time worker on the National Minimum Wage ($26.44/hour, 38 hours/week), the annual gross is about $52,254.80. After tax and Medicare, the take‑home pay is roughly $41,000‑42,000 per year. See our [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home) page for more details.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. Multiply your weekly gross by 2. For the National Minimum Wage, that’s $2,009.80 per fortnight. Use this figure to compare with your budget or loan applications.

## Average Pay Comparisons

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 show:
- Full‑time adult ordinary time: $2,083.70 per week
- All employees total earnings (including part‑time): $1,579.20 per week

These are averages, not medians for any specific job. Our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page explains how to interpret them.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026‑27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025‑26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026‑27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

## Conclusion

Understanding your hourly rate to annual conversion is straightforward with the 38‑hour week formula. Minimum wage us workers rely on the National Minimum Wage or award rates. Use our calculator and the [about the timesheet](/about) to get a personalised estimate. Always check your award and consult a professional for exact figures.
